statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 5% (low), Stress 38% (moderate), Confidence 85% (high). Every hour of the published horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no live Nasdaq-100 price path exists to score.
recommendation: Tail is published at a closed-venue floor and the mapped policy state remains EA_ON across all 24 published hours. No danger window is published, because no venue quotes at any point in the horizon and there is therefore no evidence-based interval to flag. The forward checkpoints all sit beyond the final published hour: the Sunday 22:00 UTC CME restart, fifteen hours after the horizon ends, where Friday's hawkish payroll repricing and the accumulated Strait of Hormuz energy premium would be expressed as a single opening gap rather than as an observable path; the US Labor Day holiday on Monday 7 September, which delays the first full US cash session to Tuesday 8 September; and the resumption of the macro calendar with PPI and jobless claims on 10 September and CPI on 11 September ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC meeting. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain unaffected by this publication, and later cycles will score the reopening against live evidence rather than assumptions carried from Friday.
headline: Nasdaq-100 idle at 29,544.15 with CME futures settled since Friday 21:00 UTC; the full 24-hour horizon ends before the Sunday restart, so Tail holds a closed-venue floor while hawkish rate pricing and a widening Hormuz energy premium accumulate unpriced
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having opened at 29,539.57, extended to 29,655.22, fully retraced that advance to a 29,440.15 low and recovered into the cash close. Retracement occurred repeatedly in both directions, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. The August employment report, verified against the Bureau of Labor Statistics release, showed nonfarm payrolls up 162,000 against a consensus near 55,000, the unemployment rate unchanged at 4.1%, average hourly earnings up 0.3% on the month to $37.75 and 3.1% on the year, and upward revisions of 11,000 to June and 44,000 to July. Reporting placed the priced probability of a quarter-point increase at the 15-16 September FOMC meeting near 58%, up from roughly 49% the previous day, with the 2-year yield rising toward 4.37% while the 10-year was little changed near 4.77%; the H.15 release confirms 4.34% and 4.77% through 3 September. The session's internals were split rather than aligned: the Nasdaq-100 rose while the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.29%, the S&P 500 fell 0.38% and the Dow fell 0.51%, with the narrow index carried by memory and semiconductor leadership as Micron gained about 4% and SanDisk more than 5% on AI memory demand signals. Conflicting breadth of that kind reduces directional conviction and lifts Stress; it is not evidence of the one-way path Tail is defined against. The VIX settled at 14.53 inside a 13.80-14.58 range, indicating that the options market did not price disorderly repricing even on a hot payroll day. The material unpriced input is energy: WTI is quoted near $91.48 and Brent near $96.28 after a weekly gain above 9%, the strongest week since mid-July, driven by a Strait of Hormuz crisis in which the waterway remains effectively closed to commercial shipping and both US and Iranian strikes were reported during the week ending 4 September. That premium is a persistent, already-known condition rather than a fresh discontinuity, and it accumulates across the halt without a quoting equity venue to absorb it. Every hour of this horizon, from 09:00 UTC on Saturday 5 September to 08:00 UTC on Sunday 6 September, falls inside the CME weekend halt, which closed at 21:00 UTC on Friday and reopens at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, fifteen hours after the final published slot. Tail is therefore held at a 4-5% closed-venue floor throughout, Stress drifts from 38% to 45% to reflect the accumulating rate and energy repricing awaiting the restart, and Confidence decays from 85% to 76% purely as Friday's verified evidence ages.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the second half of the August payroll session and the first twelve hours of the weekend halt. Tail ran 16-17% with Stress climbing from 59 to 62 through the pre-release European hours, peaked at Tail 24% and Stress 76% in the 12:00 UTC release hour under an event/whipsaw mode as the 162,000 payroll print landed against a consensus near 55,000, then decayed through the US cash session as the index fully retraced its highs and recovered. Mode moved to mixed from 15:00 UTC as semiconductor leadership diverged from a softer broad tape, and by 20:00 UTC Tail was 12% with Stress at 48%. From the 21:00 UTC CME settle the assessment moved to a closed-venue floor of Tail 5% and Stress 38%, held unchanged through the overnight and early Saturday hours. No hour required a mapped state beyond WATCH.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any published hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-venue floor, easing to 4% through the dormant middle of the weekend and returning to 5% as the horizon tracks back toward the venue timeline. Stress drifts from 38% to 45%, crossing into the elevated band only in the final hours, reflecting hawkish September rate-path pricing and a Strait of Hormuz energy premium that has lifted crude more than 9% on the week and is carried unpriced across the halt. Confidence decays from 85% to 76% as Friday's verified evidence ages. The Sunday 22:00 UTC restart, the Monday US Labor Day holiday, and the 8 September cash session all fall beyond the final published hour and will be scored by later cycles against live evidence.
